title: PERFORM THRU spans multiple paragraphs — flow control with implicit exit
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. INVOICE-POST.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-AMOUNT          PIC 9(7)V99.
       01  WS-TAX             PIC 9(7)V99.
       01  WS-TOTAL           PIC 9(7)V99.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
      *> PERFORM CALC-TAX THRU CALC-TOTAL executes EVERY paragraph
      *> from CALC-TAX through CALC-TOTAL inclusive, in source order.
      *> The intermediate paragraph LOG-PARTIAL is invoked even though
      *> its name does not appear in the PERFORM. Reordering source
      *> paragraphs to suit a reviewer's taste silently changes
      *> behaviour.
           PERFORM CALC-TAX THRU CALC-TOTAL
           DISPLAY WS-TOTAL
           STOP RUN.

       CALC-TAX.
           COMPUTE WS-TAX = WS-AMOUNT * 0.08.

       LOG-PARTIAL.
           DISPLAY "Tax computed: " WS-TAX.

       CALC-TOTAL.
           COMPUTE WS-TOTAL = WS-AMOUNT + WS-TAX.
notes:
PERFORM ... THRU ... runs *every* paragraph between the two labels
in source order. A naive Java/C# port that translates each
paragraph to a method and replaces PERFORM-THRU with a sequence of
calls -- without inlining the intermediate paragraphs -- silently
drops behaviour. A safe rewrite must either (a) preserve the
in-order call chain or (b) refuse-to-port without SME sign-off.
Calibrated against a public-domain batch-posting sample where
LOG-PARTIAL was inserted between CALC-TAX and CALC-TOTAL years
after the original author left.
